evaluations.evidence: view a list of sponsors
evaluations.rationale: Viewing sponsors does not inherently require another backlog story to be implemented first; sponsor data can exist independently of other described features.

evaluations.evidence: view a list of user profiles
evaluations.rationale: Listing user profiles inherently depends on having user accounts/profiles created via a registration/account capability.

evaluations.evidence: email all the trainers at once from the website
evaluations.rationale: Bulk emailing trainers can be implemented as a standalone admin function; it does not inherently require another specific story to exist first.

evaluations.evidence: have a very clear map where the buildings and rooms are
evaluations.rationale: A map page/feature can be delivered independently without requiring another story’s functionality.

evaluations.evidence: edit my training node myself
evaluations.rationale: Editing a training node presupposes that training nodes exist and are presented/managed elsewhere; this depends on training offerings being created/listed.

evaluations.evidence: limit to one registration per day per authenticated user
evaluations.rationale: This constraint depends on having an authenticated user account and a registration workflow to apply the limit to.

evaluations.evidence: admin view that helps track registration status for each attendee
evaluations.rationale: Tracking registration status inherently depends on an attendee registration process and stored registration records.

evaluations.evidence: be added to a training waitlist
evaluations.rationale: A waitlist only makes sense in the context of training registration/capacity management; it depends on a training registration workflow.

evaluations.evidence: must accept the cancellation terms with a checkbox
evaluations.rationale: Acceptance of cancellation terms is inherently part of a registration/cancellation workflow and depends on that workflow existing.

evaluations.evidence: tie in a cancellation deadline to whatever registration / cancellation workflow exists
evaluations.rationale: This story explicitly depends on an existing registration/cancellation workflow.

evaluations.evidence: add to "my schedule" if there is a schedule feature on the site
evaluations.rationale: Adding items to 'my schedule' inherently depends on the existence of a schedule feature.

evaluations.evidence: see which trainings I have signed up for
evaluations.rationale: Seeing signed-up trainings depends on having a training signup/registration capability that records those signups.

evaluations.evidence: view ... attached to their training node that shows all attendee information
evaluations.rationale: Showing attendee information for a training depends on training nodes existing and on attendees having registered for that training.

evaluations.evidence: admin view where all trainee information is shown and can be filtered to show a single training session
evaluations.rationale: Filtering trainee info by training session depends on training sessions existing and on trainee registration data being captured.

evaluations.evidence: dedicated page for each class ... link to register for class
evaluations.rationale: A class detail page can be implemented as a standalone feature; it may link to registration but does not inherently require another story to exist to be deliverable.

evaluations.evidence: link to full details of the training
evaluations.rationale: This one-page list explicitly requires a separate full-details page for trainings to link to.

evaluations.evidence: training landing page ... and a list of all training offerings
evaluations.rationale: Listing all training offerings depends on training offerings existing as content (e.g., class pages).

evaluations.evidence: link on the home page to a list of training options
evaluations.rationale: A link to a list of training options depends on that list/landing page existing.

evaluations.evidence: find out where the coding lounge is and what time it is open
evaluations.rationale: Providing location/hours information can be implemented independently as content or a page.

evaluations.evidence: refund sponsorship money that was processed via stripe
evaluations.rationale: Refunding sponsorship payments depends on having sponsorship payments processed/recorded in the first place.

evaluations.evidence: find a link on the sponsorships page to become a $350 level sponsor
evaluations.rationale: This depends on the existence of a sponsorships page and a flow to become/pay as a $350 sponsor.

evaluations.evidence: list of attendees associated with this company
evaluations.rationale: Associating attendees with a company/sponsor depends on having attendee accounts and a company sponsorship entity to associate them to.

evaluations.evidence: identify myself as and pay for a $350 company sponsorship
evaluations.rationale: Paying for sponsorship inherently depends on having a payment processing capability for sponsorships.

evaluations.evidence: create and maintain venues
evaluations.rationale: Venue CRUD can be implemented as a standalone administrative capability.

evaluations.evidence: view venue details
evaluations.rationale: Viewing venue details depends on venues being created/maintained.

evaluations.evidence: sessions associated with sponsor attendees
evaluations.rationale: This requires (1) sponsor-attendee associations and (2) sessions and their association to attendees.

evaluations.evidence: See a payment page ... as the third step of the registration process
evaluations.rationale: A third-step payment page inherently depends on the preceding registration steps existing.

evaluations.evidence: assign sponsors to events, trainings and summits
evaluations.rationale: Assigning sponsors to events/trainings/summits depends on sponsors and those entities (events/trainings/summits) existing.

evaluations.evidence: see all events, trainings and summits that a sponsor is sponsoring
evaluations.rationale: This depends on sponsors being assigned to events/trainings/summits.

evaluations.evidence: Enter payment information and have my card charged for an individual sponsorship
evaluations.rationale: Charging for an individual sponsorship depends on the user being offered/choosing an individual sponsorship as part of the registration flow.

evaluations.evidence: link BADCamp attendees to my sponsorship page
evaluations.rationale: Linking attendees to a sponsorship page depends on attendee accounts existing and a sponsorship page/profile existing.

evaluations.evidence: update my user profile
evaluations.rationale: Updating a user profile inherently depends on having a user account/profile created.

evaluations.evidence: sign up for the BADCamp newsletter
evaluations.rationale: Newsletter signup can be implemented independently without requiring other backlog stories.

evaluations.evidence: tag my blog posts
evaluations.rationale: Tagging blog posts depends on blog posts existing to be tagged.

evaluations.evidence: create blog posts
evaluations.rationale: Creating blog posts is self-contained and does not inherently require another story.

evaluations.evidence: read the blog
evaluations.rationale: Reading the blog depends on blog posts being created/published.

evaluations.evidence: sponsor a summit
evaluations.rationale: Sponsoring a summit depends on summits existing to be sponsored.

evaluations.evidence: register for a summit
evaluations.rationale: Registering for a summit depends on summits being defined/listed.

evaluations.evidence: get detailed directions to the summit venue
evaluations.rationale: Directions to a summit venue depend on summit venue/location details being provided for the summit.

evaluations.evidence: see what summits I'm signed up for
evaluations.rationale: Seeing signed-up summits depends on the ability to register for summits and store those registrations.

evaluations.evidence: see a list of attendees signed up for my summit
evaluations.rationale: This depends on summit registrations being possible and recorded.

evaluations.evidence: list basic information about my summit
evaluations.rationale: Creating/listing summit basic information can be implemented independently as summit content management.

evaluations.evidence: list sponsors for my summit
evaluations.rationale: Listing sponsors for a summit depends on having sponsors and a way to associate them with the summit.

evaluations.evidence: list an agenda for my summit
evaluations.rationale: An agenda is inherently tied to an existing summit entity to attach the agenda to.

evaluations.evidence: see how many seats are left for the summit
evaluations.rationale: Seats remaining depends on summit registration/capacity tracking being implemented.

evaluations.evidence: see specific details on summits
evaluations.rationale: Summit details pages depend on summits being defined with basic information.

evaluations.evidence: see a list of all the summits
evaluations.rationale: Listing all summits depends on summits existing as content.

evaluations.evidence: learn about sponsorship levels
evaluations.rationale: A page describing sponsorship levels can be implemented independently as content.

evaluations.evidence: use a WYSIWYG editor for all long-form content
evaluations.rationale: Providing a WYSIWYG editor is a cross-cutting capability but does not inherently depend on another specific story being implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: Link to my sponsorship profile from my job listings
evaluations.rationale: Linking from job listings to a sponsorship profile depends on both job listings existing and sponsorship profiles existing.

evaluations.evidence: learn about posting jobs as a sponsor and contact the sponsorship person
evaluations.rationale: Providing information/contact instructions can be implemented independently as content.

evaluations.evidence: post a job
evaluations.rationale: Job posting can be implemented as a standalone feature without requiring another specific story first.

evaluations.evidence: view the job board
evaluations.rationale: Viewing a job board depends on jobs being posted/available to display.

evaluations.evidence: assign a room to a time slot and a location, so that I can populate the schedule
evaluations.rationale: Populating the schedule via room/time-slot assignment depends on having a schedule feature to populate.

evaluations.evidence: see the schedule
evaluations.rationale: A schedule view can be implemented as a standalone feature (even if initially empty); it does not inherently require another story to exist first.

evaluations.evidence: see the final list of sessions approved
evaluations.rationale: A final list of approved sessions depends on sessions being accepted/approved through an acceptance process.

evaluations.evidence: bulk approve sessions as accepted
evaluations.rationale: Bulk approving sessions depends on sessions having been submitted and existing to approve.

evaluations.evidence: mark a session as accepted
evaluations.rationale: Marking a session accepted depends on sessions having been submitted and existing to mark.

evaluations.evidence: receive a notification when sessions have been evaluated
evaluations.rationale: Notifications about evaluation depend on a session submission and evaluation/acceptance process occurring.

evaluations.evidence: receive a notification when I submit a session
evaluations.rationale: This notification depends on the ability to submit a session.

evaluations.evidence: edit my session
evaluations.rationale: Editing a session depends on a session having been submitted/created.

evaluations.evidence: register to speak at BADCamp, so that I submit a session
evaluations.rationale: Registering to speak is explicitly for the purpose of submitting a session and depends on a session submission capability.

evaluations.evidence: submit a session at BADCAMP
evaluations.rationale: Submitting a session as an authenticated user depends on having user registration/account creation.

evaluations.evidence: personalize my sponsorship page
evaluations.rationale: Personalizing a sponsorship page depends on a sponsorship page/profile existing for the sponsor.

evaluations.evidence: see a list of all the summits that include when they are
evaluations.rationale: Listing summits with dates depends on summits existing with basic information.

evaluations.evidence: offered several choices of idividual sponsorship on the second page of registration
evaluations.rationale: A second page of registration inherently depends on a registration process existing (including a first page/step).

evaluations.evidence: find a link in the menu that links to the registration form
evaluations.rationale: A menu link to the registration form depends on the registration form existing.

evaluations.evidence: fill out a user registration form
evaluations.rationale: User registration/account creation is self-contained and does not inherently depend on another story.

evaluations.evidence: find session information
evaluations.rationale: Finding session information depends on sessions being submitted/available and/or approved to be displayed.
